## Summary

Ericsson, legally Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson, was founded in Stockholm in 1876 by Lars Magnus Ericsson and is headquartered in Kista, Stockholm; the Wallenberg family's Investor AB and AB Industrivärden hold the largest voting stakes [1]. It makes telecom operator infrastructure: radio base stations, radio network controllers, mobile switching centres, 4G and 5G radio access networks, IP and optical transport, and managed services [1]. Its handset business went into the Sony Ericsson joint venture in 2001, and Ericsson sold its stake to Sony in 2012 [1].

The IEEE registry lists 29 MA-L blocks to "Ericsson AB" at Torshamnsgatan in Stockholm, plus older blocks under "Ericsson", "Ericsson Group", "Ericsson, EAB/RWI/K" and "Ericsson - North America"; the "Ericsson Television Limited", "Ericsson-LG Enterprise" and "LG-Ericsson Co.,Ltd." blocks are separate registrants not covered here [2]. A MAC in an Ericsson block is therefore most likely carrier network equipment, not a consumer device, though no source consulted ties a specific product to a specific block [1][2].

The best-known security incident involving its equipment is the 2004-2005 Greek wiretapping case, in which more than 100 phones on Vodafone Greece were tapped through rogue software on four Ericsson AXE exchanges [3]. Ericsson's PSIRT publishes security bulletins and the company is a CVE Numbering Authority [4]. The 2019 settlement of over 1 billion US dollars with the US DOJ over bribery, and the 2022 leaked files on payments in Iraq, are corporate conduct cases rather than product security [1]. Silicon, FCC grantee codes and randomization are not documented here; the FCC ID databases refused requests from the session that wrote this entry.
